credit.name: yangqi0
credit.note: The original PetitGPT research checkpoint and architecture are the inspiration for this on-device lab. This repository is a WebGPU port, Q4 packer, and multi-model harness — not a replacement of that work.

models.name: PetitGPT research-v1
models.blurb: The original lab model. Tiny Llama-style GQA, trained as a small language-model research project. Reference baseline.
models.story: GitHub user yangqi0 trained PetitGPT as a small language-model research project on a single RTX 4090 with roughly 13B pretraining token positions: a 124.6M Llama-style decoder (pre-norm RMSNorm, grouped-query attention 9/3, RoPE, SwiGLU, tied embeddings) released Apache-2.0. This lab is a WebGPU port of that architecture and checkpoint — not a replacement of that work. It is usually the fastest model in the pack and the reference baseline the others are measured against.

models.name: SmolLM2 135M Instruct
models.defaultSystem: You are a helpful AI assistant named SmolLM, trained by Hugging Face
models.blurb: Hugging Face's 2025 small instruct model. Same 30×576 GQA shape, trained on 2T tokens then SFT.
models.story: SmolLM2 is the second-generation small-model line from Hugging Face’s Smol Models Research (Loubna Ben Allal and colleagues), released 2025, Apache-2.0. The 135M instruct checkpoint was pretrained on about 2 trillion tokens, then instruction-tuned. Same 30×576 GQA shape as PetitGPT, so it is a fair accuracy-vs-speed comparison: slower (larger vocab, ChatML), usually much better on the objective suite.

models.name: SmolLM 135M Instruct
models.defaultSystem: You are a helpful AI assistant named SmolLM, trained by Hugging Face
models.blurb: Previous-generation SmolLM instruct. Same size class, 600B pretrain tokens.
models.story: The first SmolLM generation from Hugging Face (2024, Apache-2.0), pretrained on a Cosmopedia / FineWeb-style mix of about 600 billion tokens, then instruction-tuned. Same 135M class as SmolLM2. Keep it if you want to see what a year of data and recipe changes bought in SmolLM2.

models.name: L20-Edu 135M
models.blurb: Same Llama-style 135M recipe, trained on one NVIDIA L20 with ~13B tokens. An auditable small-budget counterpart.
models.story: AliceYin trained this 135M Llama-style model on a single NVIDIA L20 with about 13 billion tokens (Apache-2.0). It is an educational, small-budget counterpart to the Hugging Face 135M runs: same shape, far less pretraining compute. Expect weaker answers; the point is an auditable “what one GPU can do” checkpoint.

models.name: SmolLM2 360M Instruct
models.defaultSystem: You are a helpful AI assistant named SmolLM, trained by Hugging Face
models.blurb: Larger instruct model in the same family. Slower, usually sharper. Still Q4 in-browser.
models.story: The 360M instruct sibling in Hugging Face’s SmolLM2 family (2025, Apache-2.0): 32 layers, 960-d, still Q4 in the browser. Pretrained then instruction-tuned like the 135M. Slower to load and to decode; usually sharper on the suite. Use it when you can spare ~216 MB and want the best small Hugging Face model in this pack.

models.name: MiniMind2 104M
models.blurb: jingyaogong's from-scratch 104M Llama-style model (Apache-2.0). Small vocab, GQA 8/2.
models.story: jingyaogong built MiniMind as a from-scratch teaching project: train a tiny LLM on one consumer GPU, with open code aimed at Chinese learners. The Hugging Face MiniMind2 export (Apache-2.0) is Llama-style (16 layers × 768-d, GQA 8/2, 6.4k vocab, ChatML). Stronger in Chinese than English. Native training code has extras this decoder does not need; we ship the Llama export.

models.name: MiniMind2 Small 26M
models.blurb: 26M MiniMind2. Fastest of the set; a teaching-scale checkpoint.
models.story: The 26M MiniMind2-Small checkpoint from jingyaogong’s MiniMind line (Apache-2.0): 8 layers × 512-d, same small ChatML vocab. Fastest to download and to run. It is a teaching-scale model — expect short, shaky English and better luck with Chinese. Useful when you want the decoder path without waiting on a 80 MB file.

models.name: GPT-2 124M (nanoGPT-shaped)
models.blurb: OpenAI GPT-2 124M, the architecture nanoGPT trains. Dedicated F16 WebGPU pipeline with LayerNorm, GELU, learned positions. MIT.
models.story: GPT-2 124M is OpenAI’s February 2019 language model (Radford et al.), later re-released MIT as openai-community/gpt2. Twelve layers, LayerNorm, GELU, learned absolute positions, 50k BPE — the architecture Andrej Karpathy’s nanoGPT trains. It runs in a dedicated F16 WebGPU pipeline with n-gram loop blocking for cohesive, fluent text generation.
